questions.questionText:
Group the given nine figures into three classes based on common characteristics:

9 figures are given: 1, 2, 3 are rectilinear polygons (Triangle, Square, Pentagon); 4, 5, 6 are curved closed shapes (Circle, Ellipse, Oval); 7, 8, 9 are intersecting crossed lines.
questions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
questions.explanation: Figures 1, 2, 3 form a group of straight-line polygons. Figures 4, 5, 6 form a group of curved closed figures. Figures 7, 8, 9 form a group of open intersecting line pairs.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8, 9).
questions.memoryTip: Look for trios sharing exact geometrical invariants: 3 straight, 3 curved, 3 nested.

9 figures: 1, 4, 7 each have one figure enclosed inside another identical figure; 2, 5, 8 each have two figures bisected by a line; 3, 6, 9 each have three concentric shapes.
questions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
questions.explanation: Group (1, 4, 7) share the attribute of a shape nested inside an identical shape. Group (2, 5, 8) are divided into equal halves by a bisector. Group (3, 6, 9) have concentric nested structures.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 4, 7), (2, 5, 8), (3, 6, 9).
questions.memoryTip: Look for trios sharing exact geometrical invariants: 3 straight, 3 curved, 3 nested.

9 figures are given: 1, 2, 3 are rectilinear polygons (Triangle, Square, Pentagon); 4, 5, 6 are curved closed shapes (Circle, Ellipse, Oval); 7, 8, 9 are intersecting crossed lines.
questions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
questions.explanation: Figures 1, 2, 3 form a group of straight-line polygons. Figures 4, 5, 6 form a group of curved closed figures. Figures 7, 8, 9 form a group of open intersecting line pairs.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8, 9).
questions.memoryTip: Look for trios sharing exact geometrical invariants: 3 straight, 3 curved, 3 nested.

9 figures: 1, 4, 7 each have one figure enclosed inside another identical figure; 2, 5, 8 each have two figures bisected by a line; 3, 6, 9 each have three concentric shapes.
questions.hint: Find the 3 distinct defining characteristics that can partition the 9 figures into 3 equal sets of 3.
questions.explanation: Group (1, 4, 7) share the attribute of a shape nested inside an identical shape. Group (2, 5, 8) are divided into equal halves by a bisector. Group (3, 6, 9) have concentric nested structures.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify recurring visual properties (e.g. line type, nesting, shading).
Step 2: Form candidate triplets that share the exact same property.
Step 3: Ensure all 9 figures are exhausted without overlap to get (1, 4, 7), (2, 5, 8), (3, 6, 9).
questions.memoryTip: Look for trios sharing exact geometrical invariants: 3 straight, 3 curved, 3 nested.
